page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Cloud Native server family, built on KVM virtualization. The instance provides 20 shared vCPUs running on an AMD EPYC 7542 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.2 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware configuration does not include local disk storage, dedicated GPUs, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote attached block storage and external network provisioning.

Benchmark results demonstrate competitive multi-core capacity with some divergence between synthetic tests. The server achieved a strong Geekbench multi-core score of 16287.0 and a single-core score of 2055.0, alongside top-quartile performance in image processing (13572.0) and text processing (2664.0). Under PassMark testing, it recorded an average overall CPU score of 33209.56 and 11316.86 in database operations. Conversely, stress-ng single-core execution ranked in the bottom 10 percent at 784.29, while stress-ng multi-core reached an average 15708.05. Memory bandwidth tests yielded 69.81 GB/sec uncached read throughput and 29.73 GB/sec write throughput.

Because the 20 vCPUs are shared rather than dedicated, compute capacity is subject to potential virtualization overhead and resource contention, balanced by a dense CPU-to-memory allocation. The absence of bundled local storage places primary I/O dependencies on external volumes. This instance is best configured for parallelized background processes, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation, web serving clusters, and containerized microservices that benefit from aggregate core count without requiring continuous dedicated single-core throughput.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 20 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz and 64.0 GB of memory. Operating under KVM virtualization on the x86_64 architecture, the server delivers 3.2 GB of RAM per core with no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In synthetic evaluations, the platform demonstrates strong Geekbench multi-core (16287.0) and single-core (2055.0) outcomes, while stress-ng single-core testing falls into lower percentiles. PassMark CPU execution scored 33209.56, complemented by 10.65 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 27.79 million Redis SET operations per second. The shared core model trades guaranteed single-thread isolation for multi-core density, making the instance suitable for distributed container workloads, CI/CD runners, batch processing, and horizontally scaled web serving environments.
